content: The antibiotic clarithromycin interacts with various drugs and substances, primarily by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. These interactions can either increase or decrease the levels and effects of the co-administered drugs, potentially leading to altered therapeutic outcomes or adverse effects. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions: 1. Clarithromycin and Propafenone: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Clarithromycin and Pyridoxine: Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Clarithromycin and Quazepam: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Clarithromycin and Quetiapine: Co-administration increases the risk of QTc interval prolongation, which can lead to cardiac toxicity. Avoid use with other QT-prolonging drugs and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT intervals. Post-marketing cases have reported QT prolongation with overdose or in patients with concomitant illnesses or electrolyte imbalances. 5. Vonoprazan and Quinidine: Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is needed with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 6. Clarithromycin and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Clarithromycin also increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 7. Clarithromycin and Quizartinib: Clarithromycin increases quizartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism.
